stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Study the diagram: the domestic mains supply in Tunisia delivers an alternating voltage of effective value $U_{eff} = 230\,\text{V}$ at frequency $f = 50\,\text{Hz}$. Three wires enter the outlet: the phase (live), the neutral, and the earth. The fuse box protects the installation with a circuit breaker (disjoncteur) and a residual-current device (différentiel). Click the labels on the diagram to reveal each part.
stages.concept: The phase wire carries the alternating potential; the neutral returns the current; the earth wire (connected to a grounded rod, prise de terre) safely diverts any leakage from a metal appliance frame. The disjoncteur cuts the current on overload or short-circuit. The différentiel (30 mA) trips when phase and neutral currents differ — the sign that current is leaking through a person or a fault.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Diagram hidden. Answer each safety scenario using the concepts alone. You must answer all cards correctly in one pass — a wrong answer restarts the deck with a fresh order.
stages.concept: Two invariants to remember: (1) the earth wire's only job is to give leakage current a safer path than through you; (2) the différentiel compares phase and neutral currents — any imbalance means current is going somewhere it shouldn't.

labels.question: safety scenario
labels.peek_hint: For each card, ask: which wire or device is designed to handle that exact fault? Earth = leakage path. Différentiel = detects imbalance. Disjoncteur = overload / short. Insulation and dry skin = your own resistance.

1.1: The mains voltage is described by an effective value and a frequency — read them off the diagram.
1.2: There are three wires in a modern outlet, each with a distinct job. Click each label to see which is which.
1.3: Two devices sit in the fuse box: one for overload, one for leakage detection. Note how they differ.

2.1: For each card, identify which fault is happening: overload, short-circuit, leakage to ground, or a person becoming a path.
2.2: Then match the fault to the device or wire that was designed for it. Earth wire = safe path for leakage. Différentiel = detects current imbalance. Disjoncteur = overcurrent.
2.3: Wet skin lowers your body's resistance drastically, so a small voltage can drive a dangerous current — that is why you never touch outlets with wet hands.
